title: Structure Cmake for Cpp package managers
body:
It would be useful to be able to use MAVSDK with cpp package managers (Hunter, Conan etc) for automatic dependency resolution. Instead of depending on a `SUPERBUILD` or local dependencies.

I've been implementing this library with [hunter](https://github.com/cpp-pm/hunter) and have found success by doing the following:

0. `SUPERBUILD=OFF`
1. Remove git commands from Cmakelists.txt, such as getting version from git tags
2. Don't use git submodules 
3. Remove Find modules provided by https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/cmake/Modules/
4. Use common lib names when linking: 
`JsonCpp::jsoncpp` -> `jsoncpp_lib`
`tinyxml2::tinyxml2` -> `tinyxml2`


This won't work for `mavsdk_server` but it is a start. There is likely to be more changes to this to get it to work (for Hunter I have included Hunter_gate but obviously this differs for each manager :) )

title: set_rate missing for rawGps
body:
Hi,

rawGps info now can be accessed with v0.38+, but I found that its missing something like "telemetry.set_rate_rawGps()" as the position can do "telemetry.set_rate_position()". Is this a missing feature or there is another way to set the rawGps access rate?

Best

comments.body:
Hi, good question. You can actually just use `set_rate_gps_info` as the underlying mavlink message is the same.

@JonasVautherin should we add it nevertheless or add a comment to clarify this?

I first was thinking about adding it, and handling the case where somebody does `set_rate_gps_info()` AND `set_rate_raw_gps` like this:

* If both `subscribe_gps_info` and `subscribe_raw_gps` are active, use the max of both rate values
* If only one is active, take its rate

The problem is for the polling interface: what if I want to poll gps_info very fast, but subscribed to raw_gps at a slow rate? Or maybe something like:

* If both `subscribe_gps_info` and `subscribe_raw_gps` are active, use the max of both rate values
* If only one is active, take its rate
* If `set_rate_` has been called (even if the subscription is inactive), use that rate in the max computation

Which then means that if you do `set_rate_gps_info` and then only poll `raw_gps`, you see the effect of the new rate (if that rate was faster than the default). Not sure if that's a problem, though... And we should document the behavior, and maybe add a log line when `set_rate_` is being set to the lower value and is therefore ignored.

Not perfect, but that's the best I can think of to have a rather natural way of using both rates :sweat_smile:

title: Camera plugin uses deprecated messages
body:
The camera plugin currently uses deprecated messages like [MAV_CMD_REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION) instead of [MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE).

This would make it unusable with a camera that only supports the "new" request message.

comments.body:
I see your point, but here is my personal opinion: MAVLink "servers" should implement both in the foreseeable future, because MAVLink does not provide a way to detect which command is supported and which is not (well, there is a `MAV_CMD_ACK_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, but I don't think it is mandatory nor generally implemented, and it's not enough for `MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE` which represents subcommands).

More specifically, if we move MAVSDK to using only `MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE`, we will break all legacy systems that don't support the new way. "Deprecated" means that it may be removed in the future, not that it is not supported anymore. MAVLink still supports them, so MAVSDK should still support them (until MAVLink removes them entirely).

Now, we may be tempted to wish for a transition: after all, why not letting new servers implement only the new messages, and have MAVSDK detect which message it should use? The problem with that is that MAVLink cannot make a difference between an unsupported command and a command that timed out. It is very common for systems that don't support a command to just ignore it, and it is sometimes designed like this: only one component of the system is meant to know that command and answer to it, and the others just ignore it.

So how do you make MAVSDK detect if the new message is supported? If you send a "dummy" `MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE` and get an ACK, then you know that the drone supports this message, but what happens if it times out? Sh
...[truncated]

I agree with @JonasVautherin and this was my stance about one year ago. I think by now we can start to try using the new MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE and fallback to the previous one if it doesn't work. This might lead to suboptimal behavior for systems that don't support it yet but that might be ok in my opinion. The cameras that I'm aware off, except the ones with Yuneec H520, should support the new way.

title: Can the gRPC server be started before mavsdk-server discovers/connects to a system?
body:
In some cases, applications using mavsdk may start before the UAV system starts and is discovered by the mavsdk-server. In this case, clients intending to connect to the mavsdk-server will effectively have to block because the gRPC port will not be available.

Alternatively, if the gRPC server is up and the port is available, the clients won't have to block and the channels that are running in the background will automatically start receiving data once the UAV system is discovered.

The earlier versions of the mavsdk-server used to behave in the same manner which made client-side implementation quite easy.

comments.body: Yeah it used to be that mavsdk would create a "dummy" system to receive subscriptions and whatnot, but that's not the case anymore. So your app has to wait until the drone is discovered before it can start the subscriptions. `mavsdk-server` is just reflecting that :innocent:

That won't work because the server implementation now needs to discover a drone. If you do that, your subscriptions won't ever have an effect because mavsdk won't save them for when a system is discovered.

Unfortunately I think that you have to deal with that on your side...
Oh. I hadn't noticed when I was testing it because SITL was always there. Maybe I can make some changes to MAVSDK-Java so that the API works the same as before.

In my opinion, a very good next step for MAVSDK-Java would be to remove the dependency on gRPC and use direct bindings instead (i.e. JNI), so that it would be much more lightweight. But it also means that the API would get closer to the C++ API, which does not allow that at the moment.

And there you would see why this is problematic: MAVSDK-C++ supports discovering multiple drones, so if you subscribe to, say, the position updates before a drone is known, then MAVSDK cannot know if you were meaning to subscribe to the first or to the second drone that appears. That's why this is delegated to the user, because they know their use-case (and MAVSDK doesn't) :grin:.

Yes indeed, and that would be an interesting project to take up. We not only use MAVSDK-Java for the Android GCS, but also on companion computers running our headless Java framework. And this would definitely give a performance boost to it.

But for now, I was thinking of altering some logic in the plugin wrappers that can give users a bit more flexibility without them having to worry about initialisation problems while keeping the API as simple as it was before. That certainly helped me a lot in adopting the library. And then we can look into JNI and multiple system support. I'll try to create a PR soon.

title: Using MAVSDK with only Iridium connection
body:
Hi! I'm building a drone that would only have a SATCOM connection to it. And I want to be able to send commands to it using SATCOM. And while testing with MAVSDK I notice that it seems to require a connection to PX4 before being able to send MAVLink commands, is that correct? 

So I was wondering if it is possible to put the MAVSDK_server into a mode that would only give back the MAVLink string (in hex) so I can then send it through the SATCOM website and communicate with my drone. I would also like reverse path also, so decoding a MAVLink string and return a human-readable string.

Thanks in advance!

comments.body:
> it seems to require a connection to PX4 before being able to send MAVLink commands, is that correct?

* When you start the connection with `udp://:14540`, it's equivalent to `udp://0.0.0.0:14540`, and it says "have MAVSDK _listen_ (/bind to) on 14540". In that mode, the drone must send MAVLink messages to MAVSDK on port 14540.
* When you start the connection with `udp://192.168.1.12:14555`, then it tells MAVSDK to start sending MAVLink heartbeats to the drone (here `192.168.1.12`) on port 14555. In that mode, the drone must listen (bind) to 14555.

Note that I invented the IPs and ports, you can use whatever you want. The point is just that `udp://:<port>` and `udp://0.0.0.0:<port>` run mavsdk in "server" mode, and `udp://<some_ip>:<port>` run mavsdk in "client" mode.

Does that help?

Hi @JonasVautherin! I'm familiar with the concept of using the UDP connection and port in general. But I'm more asking where the drone is only able to communicate with it through SATCOM, something like Iridium. So there's no real interface possible, either through UDP or Serial. Imagine that the drone is at 60 000ft (or 25 km) of altitude :sweat_smile: and we want to send and receive MAVLink messages. There's already the Iridium driver in PX4, but I need to add the part that decode and encode those messages.  

In an ideal world, I'd like that the MAVSDK_server should just generate it's MAVLink message for the command I'm asking it for and would decode a MAVLink message that I've provided to it. We want to put that MAVSDK_server in our backend. Let me know if that's more clear :)!

Oh... sorry I read too quickly :sweat_smile:. I don't know if it would make sense to add support for Iridium in MAVSDK, but could you make a bridge, say like this?

```
[------ on the ground -----]                                                [--- on the drone ---]
MAVSDK <--- udp ---> bridge     <------------ Iridium --------------->       drone
```

So you write your UDP-to-Iridium bridge on the ground, and connect MAVSDK to it over UDP. For MAVSDK, it's just a UDP connection, and the drone just receives MAVLink messages.

Then the question would be whether or not MAVSDK generates too much traffic for your connection, I guess?

No worries, and I wasn't able to add a label to the issue, but it was more of a question towards MAVSDK if it was possible or not. So if it doesn't fit into the design that's alright, I'm more looking at a solution for what I want to do :).

As per your suggestion, that might be a good idea. In the Iridium driver in the PX4 documentation, they actually recommend something similar to what you're suggesting (http://docs.px4.io/main/en/advanced_features/satcom_roadblock.html#overview), here's the diagram:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12837376/215919420-4edb8f49-d067-4d22-81d1-a0324c8956a7.png)

But we really want to control what's going out of the MAVSDK_server, like on the PX4 we are only allowing some MAVLink streams  going out of the SATCOM since sending through SATCOM is costly : /.

I'd really like to use MAVSDK for this, but I'm unsure if it's a good fit, since I want something more like an encoder/decoder for MAVLink. Maybe I can just add a mode when starting the MAVSDK_server where it's kind of offline and behave differently?

Basically MAVSDK expects some heartbeats from the drone. Are you saying you would not have heartbeats? If so, we would have to make a config option that allows to have the timeout much bigger. 

However, you sorta need to discover a system initially, otherwise you don't know what the target system ID and target component ID to send a command to.

MAVSDK also does a bit of initial back and forth to get some basic information. We would have to have some "low bandwidth" mode to avoid all that but it would require some work.

It feels quite specific, I'm not sure if it would fit in MAVSDK. It sounds like you really need to control what goes out of MAVSDK, so anyway I would personally do that with a proxy. Still it may be worth using MAVSDK instead of re-implementing the protocols (e.g. mission transfer, commands, etc).

You can already increase the timeout for commands in MAVSDK. Then for the heartbeat, one way would be to have your proxy "pretend to be the drone" and send regular heartbeats to MAVSDK (say your proxy sends a heartbeat every second, and receives the heartbeats from the drone at whatever rate you want). Same for others, like the parameters: you could maybe have a cache in your proxy, in order to save round-trips.

> MAVSDK also does a bit of initial back and forth to get some basic information.

I also would like to know the minimal set of messages that MAVSDK needs to get started. It needs the heartbeats, and then at least a few params (I think). I may get to make a list in the next couple of weeks, so that could help. If you do before me, feel free to share it here :blush:

Hi @julianoes! 
> Basically MAVSDK expects some heartbeats from the drone. Are you saying you would not have heartbeats? If so, we would have to make a config option that allows to have the timeout much bigger.

We would mainly use a modified version of the [HIGH_LATENCY2](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#HIGH_LATENCY2) for most of our communication with the GCS. So they would act as heartbeat for us.

> However, you sorta need to discover a system initially, otherwise you don't know what the target system ID and target component ID to send a command to.
MAVSDK also does a bit of initial back and forth to get some basic information. We would have to have some "low bandwidth" mode to avoid all that but it would require some work.

Yeah, that was my understanding while using it with the PX4 SITL. And that was a motivation behind the questions I'm asking. I feel like MAVSDK is more supported for PX4 than the alternatives, but I wanted to know if it does what I want it to do :sweat_smile:.

> It feels quite specific, I'm not sure if it would fit in MAVSDK. It sounds like you really need to control what goes out of MAVSDK, so anyway I would personally do that with a proxy. Still it may be worth using MAVSDK instead of re-implementing the protocols (e.g. mission transfer, commands, etc).

Yeah, I've been looking around and like I told Julian, I felt like MAVSDK was more supported for PX4 than the alternative, but I think you are right. It doesn't sound like MAVSDK fit well with my use case. For the project I'm working on, it is more about just translating the MAVLink messages, so maybe [pymavlink](https://github.com/ArduPilot/pymavlink) would fit better there. I need to look more into it. If you have other idea regarding simply encoding and decoding MAVLink message, please let me know :grin:!

Thanks a lot for the information, guys!

title: Server plugin should not receive commands that are addressed to other components.
body:
Hi!

I'm working on multiple cameras using [mavlink camera protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/camera.html) as it is [not supported so far](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_camera.html).

While browsing the source code I've noticed, that it seems the **component_id** field is missing in MAVLinkCommandIntHandlerTableEntry and MAVLinkCommandLongHandlerTableEntry which may be used to filter out commands sent to another component in a system (in a similar way as it is implemented for mavlink_message_handler)

As for now every camera server will process and react to all commands regardless if the component ID matches its own_component_id. For example, if I select camera and subscribe to video_stream_info - all cameras will send ack and video_stream_info message, which seems wrong to me.
This may be simply fixed as it is done [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/30825da62876b8437a9c06f11fe6ad77d79c8136/src/mavsdk/plugins/tracking_server/tracking_server_impl.cpp#L316):
But I'm not sure if this is the right place/level where it has to be done.

Many thanks!

Best regards,
Alex

comments.body:
Thanks for the issue. I think I understand the issue but disagree on the implementation change that you suggest.

The issue is that a server plugin is tied to a component in the first place, so it should not receive commands that are addressed to other components.

The filtering is supposed to happen somewhere in [mavsdk_impl.cpp](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/30825da62876b8437a9c06f11fe6ad77d79c8136/src/mavsdk/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L414) but it's not. I think you're right that components receive all messages, even if they are targeted at other components only.

It looks like that the message handler has the appropriate interface:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/973c663f9776130cce9f3cc7b05cb432c4f16254/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_message_handler.cpp#L26

but it's not used. We need to find a way to use it from server components.
Turns out this component ID filter is to filter for source, for multiple camera plugins (not camera server plugins).

Having looked at this a bit more it looks like your suggestion was pretty close. We don't actually have to add the component ID into the handler table because we can get it from the parent server component.

Can you check if https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2270 fixes your problem?

Many thanks for such quick feedback!

>> The issue is that a server plugin is tied to a component in the first place, so it should not receive commands that are addressed to other components.

That is correct, I've renamed the issue so it does not contain my implementation details and assumptions.

>> Can you check if https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2270 fixes your problem?

It does! 

Best regards,
Alex

title: libmavsdk.so exports statically linked curl/openssl symbols causing conflicts with ROS2 FastDDS middleware
body:
Hi!. I've read that MavSDK is not really supposed to be used with ROS2 but nevertheless, I'd like to share a problem that I've found. 

When running a node with MavSDK under the hood (C++), I've been getting instant seg-faults until I switched from `rmw_fastrtps` to `rmw_zenoh_cpp`. I've tried to dig into the problem using AI since I don't really understand such a low-level subject.

It provides the following explanation:

1. Problem: MAVSDK exports its statically linked curl symbols into the global dynamic linker namespace. When used alongside ROS2 with rmw_fastrtps_cpp, FastDDS resolves its curl calls to MAVSDK's internal version, causing a segfault in XMLProfileManager::loadDefaultXMLFile() at address 0xA.
2. Proof command:
```bash
nm -D /lib/libmavsdk.so.3 | grep "^[0-9a-f]* T curl_"
```
This shows curl symbols exported as public (T = global text symbol). They should be local/hidden.
The output of the command attached.

I'm a big fan of both MavSDK and ROS2 so I would appreciate the fix so I will able to use them without any workarounds.

Thank you for your work gentlemen!

[output.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26314048/output.txt)
